1. Approach and rationale

The current issue is that high-dimensional first-order smoothing solvers tend to descend very quickly into a local plateau of the exact max-over-lag objective and then become insensitive to the small analytic mismatch needed to reach `C5 <= 0.381042` or better. The goal here is to preserve the advantageous parent while extracting additional value from the exact discrete evaluator using a different update primitive.

The proposed algorithm is neither a purely convex relaxation nor a direct ``put all of this into SLSQP again'' method. The central idea is a geometrical local improvement procedure that:

- uses only feasible two-coordinate moves that preserve the exact sum constraint and box bounds;
- builds, for each candidate move, a quadratic surrogate of the full two-sign finite-support correlation coefficient by interpolation from three exact evaluations;
- constructs one-dimensional candidate line-search values that include the medians of the model components and important endpoint candidates;
- accepts moves only after exact re-evaluation with the authoritative scalar `max(np.correlate(h, 1-h, full))*dx`;
- repeats locally, then adds stochastic large-neighborhood perturbations around the incumbent while preserving reasoning to the supplied construction. If no improvement is found, searches other nearby resolutions derived algorithmically from the parent.

Why it can improve the supplied parent: previous multi-start high-dimensional tangent projections are mostly forcing all active profiles to co-evolve together; feasible two- and three-coordinate moves are considerably simpler dynamics and can pass across plateaus, while the quadratic interpolation captures the exact profile derivative, plus the no-der actor predictor so `∂ / ∂h_i` sign conventions are not silently swapped by the `template-errors` peculiarity; the method is constructed out of the evaluation array itself.
